`write_loop()` generates copy-pasteable R code for a for-loop simulation that confirms the analytical power calculation.
The simulation uses potential outcomes with a constant additive treatment effect and HC2 robust standard errors (via the sandwich package).

## Running the pipeline

Suppose we plan to replicate @Ahler2018, who find that correcting respondents' misperceptions of their out-party reduces affective polarization.
The standard deviation of feeling thermometer responses in the 2020 ANES is 20.8.
We plan to recruit 500 respondents per condition and assume a treatment effect of 3 points (the lower bound of Ahler and Sood's 95% confidence interval).

```{r}
library(powerrules)

result <- from_sd(sd_y = 20.8) |>
  find_power(n = 500, tau = 3)
```

## Generating the simulation code

`write_loop()` takes the result and prints a self-contained simulation script:

```{r}
write_loop(result)
```

## Running the generated code

The simulation runs 500 experiments with one-sided tests (size 0.05 for 90% CIs), matching Rule 2 from @Rainey_2026 exactly.
The simulated power should be close to the analytical 74% from powerrules.

```{r}
library(sandwich)  # for HC2 robust SEs

# --- Parameters ---
n    <- 500    # respondents per condition
tau  <- 3      # treatment effect
sd_y <- 20.8   # SD(Y) in control group

# --- Simulate 500 experiments ---
n_sims <- 500
set.seed(1234)
reject <- logical(n_sims)

for (i in seq_len(n_sims)) {
  # Potential outcomes: constant, additive treatment effect
  y0 <- rnorm(2 * n, mean = 0, sd = sd_y)
  y1 <- y0 + tau

  # Complete random assignment: n to each condition
  z <- sample(rep(0:1, each = n))

  # Reveal observed outcome
  y <- ifelse(z == 1, y1, y0)

  # Estimate via OLS with HC2 robust SEs
  fit <- lm(y ~ z)
  est <- coef(fit)["z"]
  se  <- sqrt(vcovHC(fit, type = "HC2")["z", "z"])

  # One-sided p-value and size-0.05 test
  p_val <- pnorm(est / se, lower.tail = FALSE)
  reject[i] <- p_val < 0.05
}

cat("Simulated power:", round(mean(reject) * 100), "%\n")
cat("Expected:       ~74%\n")
```
